text:
Bitcoin reclaimed the $60,000 threshold on July 2, rallying 3.2% to $60,150 after the June Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report showed an increase of 114,000 jobs, precisely matching the consensus forecast. The cooling from May’s 172,000 addition, combined with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments regarding easing inflation risks, fueled short-covering in derivatives. Nonetheless, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs registered another $296 million in net outflows on July 1, with BlackRock's IBIT leading redemptions at $219 million.

In traditional finance, U.S. Treasury yields eased as the 10-year note slid from 4.50% back toward 4.47%, tracking a lower-than-expected ADP private jobs print. U.S. equity indices stabilized after a volatile start to the quarter, driven by continuing AI infrastructure spending. This moderate labor slowdown and yield stabilization have temporarily restored risk appetite, prompting a relief bounce for digital assets.
